items.stem: An 79-year-old hospitalized client develops acute fluctuating confusion consistent with delirium. For each nursing action, indicate whether it is indicated or not indicated as supportive care while the underlying cause is treated.

rows.text: Keep the room quiet and well lit, with a clock and calendar visible.
Encourage use of the client's eyeglasses and hearing aids if needed.
Apply physical restraints routinely at the first sign of restlessness.
Invite familiar family members to spend time at the bedside when appropriate.
Move the client frequently between unfamiliar rooms to provide stimulation.

rationales.R1: Indicated. Merck advises a stable, quiet, well-lit environment with visual cues such as clocks and calendars; OpenStax lists a quiet well-lit room and clocks/calendars within view.
rationales.R2: Indicated. Merck and OpenStax both support minimizing sensory deficits by ensuring eyeglasses and hearing aids are used.
rationales.R3: Not indicated. OpenStax advises avoiding restraints; Merck states physical restraints should be minimized because they can worsen agitation and injury risk.
rationales.R4: Indicated. Both sources support involving family for reorientation, familiarity, and safety.
rationales.R5: Not indicated. Frequent unfamiliar room changes increase environmental stress; Merck emphasizes a stable environment and frequent reorientation in a consistent setting.

items.stem: An older adult is admitted with new fluctuating confusion. Which factors should the nurse recognize as common precipitants or contributors to delirium? Select all that apply.

options.text: Urinary tract infection or other acute infection
Dehydration
Recently started anticholinergic or opioid medications
A lifelong gradual decline in memory over several years without acute change
Sleep deprivation during hospitalization
Stable, well-controlled hypothyroidism treated for decades with no recent change

rationales.A: Correct. Merck and OpenStax identify infection (including UTI) as a common precipitant of delirium in older adults.
rationales.B: Correct. Dehydration is listed by both Merck and OpenStax among common causes/precipitants.
rationales.C: Correct. Medications—especially anticholinergics and opioids—are leading causes of delirium in both sources.
rationales.D: Incorrect. Lifelong gradual memory decline describes dementia's slower course, not an acute delirium precipitant; delirium has sudden onset.
rationales.E: Correct. Sleep deprivation is a precipitating factor in Merck and a listed cause in OpenStax.
rationales.F: Incorrect. Long-stable treated hypothyroidism without change is not identified as an acute precipitant; acute metabolic/endocrine crises can be, but this option describes a non-acute stable state.

items.stem: An older adult reports light-headedness and near-falls when standing up from bed. Orthostatic hypotension is suspected. Which teaching best reduces orthostatic symptom risk?

options.text: Rise slowly from a lying or sitting position and pause before walking.
Stand up as quickly as possible to shorten the dizzy period.
Limit daytime fluid intake to keep blood pressure from rising.
Remain on strict bed rest for several days to rest the cardiovascular system.

rationales.A: Correct. Merck nonpharmacologic care advises patients to rise slowly from a recumbent or sitting position; OpenStax supports progressive mobilization such as dangling at the bedside before standing.
rationales.B: Incorrect. Rapid standing worsens orthostatic drops; Merck links sudden upright posture to symptoms.
rationales.C: Incorrect. Merck advises adequate fluids; fluid restriction can worsen orthostasis.
rationales.D: Incorrect. Prolonged bed rest contributes to orthostatic intolerance; Merck encourages sitting up daily and activity when feasible.

items.topic: Orthostatic hypotension — rise slowly; progressive mobilization

sources.title: Orthostatic Hypotension
sources.evidence: Patients should rise slowly from a recumbent or sitting position and consume adequate fluids; prolonged bed rest should be interrupted with sitting and exercise.

sources.title: 41.3 Health Risks for Older Adults
sources.evidence: Progressive mobilization includes dangling on the edge of the bed before sitting and ambulating.

items.stem: A toddler arrives with sudden high fever, drooling, and inspiratory stridor and is suspected to have epiglottitis. Which nursing action is the priority until a secure airway is available?

options.text: Avoid upsetting interventions such as forcing an oral exam, and keep the child as calm as possible while preparing for urgent airway management.
Immediately use a tongue blade to visualize the pharynx at the bedside.
Force the child flat supine for a full physical examination before calling for help.
Send the child alone to radiology for a neck film without airway-capable staff present.

rationales.A: Correct. Merck states airway assessment/management takes priority and that in children with stridor, upsetting interventions that could trigger obstruction should be avoided until an airway is established; visualization is not done until full respiratory support is available.
rationales.B: Incorrect. Direct visualization is deferred until full respiratory support is available because agitation can precipitate obstruction.
rationales.C: Incorrect. Children often maintain a forward sniffing/tripod posture; forcing supine and unnecessary stimulation can worsen airway compromise.
rationales.D: Incorrect. Suspected epiglottitis requires hospitalization and airway-capable management; unattended transport for imaging is unsafe.

items.topic: Epiglottitis — prioritize airway; avoid upsetting exam until support available

sources.title: Epiglottitis
sources.evidence: Visualization not until full respiratory support available; airway management paramount; avoid upsetting interventions that could trigger obstruction until airway established.

items.stem: Which presentation should lead the nurse to suspect epiglottitis rather than typical viral croup?

options.text: Sudden high fever, drooling, toxic appearance, and sitting forward without a barky cough
Gradual onset of a barky cough with mild fever after a few days of upper respiratory symptoms
Isolated nasal congestion without fever or respiratory distress
Chronic night-time cough for several weeks without acute distress

rationales.A: Correct. CPS and Merck describe epiglottitis with sudden high fever, drooling, toxic/anxious appearance, forward sniffing posture, and absence of barky cough.
rationales.B: Incorrect. That pattern fits typical croup (more gradual; barky cough characteristic).
rationales.C: Incorrect. Lacks red-flag airway findings of epiglottitis.
rationales.D: Incorrect. Chronic cough without acute toxicity is not the fulminant epiglottitis pattern.

items.stem: A charge nurse on an Ontario medical unit is assigning care that involves an unregulated care provider (UCP). Which action best reflects safe assignment based on competence?

options.text: Confirm the UCP is competent to perform the specific activity safely for this client in these circumstances before assigning it.
Assume any UCP can perform every procedure because the tasks look simple.
Assign complex unstable assessments to the UCP so the RN can finish charting.
Avoid verifying competence once the UCP has completed a general orientation week.

rationales.A: Correct. CNO requires nurses who assign to UCPs to know the UCP is competent for the particular procedure/activity for the client in the given circumstances; OpenStax Right Person requires verified education/competencies before delegation.
rationales.B: Incorrect. CNO states a nurse cannot assume a UCP is competent regardless of how straightforward a procedure appears.
rationales.C: Incorrect. OpenStax Right Circumstance requires stable clients with expected outcomes for assistive personnel; nursing assessment/judgment stays with the RN.
rationales.D: Incorrect. Competence must be known for the particular activity and circumstances, not assumed from generic orientation alone.

items.stem: Which client situation is most appropriate for an RN to assign basic assistive care to unregulated care provider (UCP/assistive personnel) under the Right Circumstance principle?

options.text: A stable client with expected outcomes who needs assistance with routine hygiene
A newly admitted client with unstable vital signs requiring continuous reassessment
A client with sudden respiratory distress needing immediate clinical judgment
A client whose condition just changed and has not yet been reassessed by the RN

rationales.A: Correct. OpenStax states patients must be stable with expected outcomes before care responsibilities are delegated to assistive personnel; CNO likewise ties UCP assignment to appropriate client circumstances and competence.
rationales.B: Incorrect. Unstable clients needing continuous RN reassessment are not appropriate for AP/UCP-led care without direct RN management.
rationales.C: Incorrect. Acute distress requires RN clinical judgment and Take Action, not assistive-only assignment.
rationales.D: Incorrect. OpenStax requires the RN to reassess after condition changes before deciding whether delegation remains appropriate.

items.stem: Which community nursing intervention is the best example of tertiary prevention?

options.text: Referring a stroke survivor to physical, occupational, and speech rehabilitation to reduce disability
Administering routine childhood immunizations to prevent vaccine-preventable disease
Organizing asymptomatic breast-cancer screening for early detection
Teaching a healthy community how to begin exercise before any disease risk factors appear

rationales.A: Correct. OpenStax defines tertiary prevention as lessening impact and preventing complications through therapies and rehabilitation; CDC describes post-stroke rehabilitation with PT/OT/speech to treat stroke effects and support recovery.
rationales.B: Incorrect. Immunization is primary prevention (prevent disease before it occurs).
rationales.C: Incorrect. Screening asymptomatic people is secondary prevention (early detection).
rationales.D: Incorrect. Primordial/primary risk-factor prevention precedes disease; it is not tertiary care of established illness.

items.stem: A nurse is teaching aspiration-prevention strategies for an older adult with dysphagia. Which actions should be included? Select all that apply.

options.text: Maintain an upright position (at least 30 degrees) during and after meals
Encourage a slow pace while eating and drinking
Support oral hygiene and dental care to reduce harmful oral bacteria
Collaborate with a speech-language pathologist for safe-swallowing strategies
Have the client eat while fully flat in bed to conserve energy
Rush meal trays so feeding finishes in under five minutes

rationales.A: Correct. OpenStax advises upright positioning at least 30 degrees during/after eating; Merck likewise elevates the head of bed >30° for aspiration-risk clients with decreased LOC.
rationales.B: Correct. OpenStax notes many patients benefit from a slow eating/drinking pace.
rationales.C: Correct. Both OpenStax and Merck support optimized oral hygiene to reduce pneumonia risk related to aspirated oral organisms.
rationales.D: Correct. OpenStax recommends SLP collaboration; Merck notes speech pathologist training in strategies such as chin tuck.
rationales.E: Incorrect. Flat positioning increases aspiration risk; upright positioning is indicated.
rationales.F: Incorrect. Rushing contradicts slow-pace guidance and increases aspiration risk.

items.stem: A float nurse arrives to help on a telemetry unit. Which charge-nurse action best applies determination of clinical ability when making assignments?

options.text: Match assignment complexity to the float nurse's demonstrated proficiency with similar tasks and current competencies
Give the float nurse the most unstable clients without reviewing competencies because all RNs have the same license
Assign tasks outside the float nurse's role description without training because the unit is short-staffed
Ignore the float nurse's current workload when adding multiple complex admissions

rationales.A: Correct. OpenStax leadership guidance requires assessing skills/competencies and matching care complexity to demonstrated proficiency with similar tasks; CNO likewise requires knowing competence for the activity and circumstances.
rationales.B: Incorrect. Shared RN licensure does not replace unit-specific competency assessment for complex unstable assignments.
rationales.C: Incorrect. OpenStax Right Task requires activities within job description/policies and training for skilled competencies.
rationales.D: Incorrect. OpenStax requires considering current workload and impact on safe care when determining clinical ability.

items.stem: An 84-year-old client becomes newly confused after several psychoactive medications are started in hospital. Which nursing action best addresses a common medication-related contributor to delirium?

options.text: Collaborate to review and minimize newly added anticholinergic or opioid medications when clinically appropriate
Add another sedative at bedtime to ensure the client sleeps through the night without reassessment
Encourage the family to bring all home anticholinergic OTC products for unrestricted use
Ignore medication review because delirium is never related to drugs in older adults

rationales.A: Correct. Merck identifies medications—particularly anticholinergics and opioids—as leading causes of delirium and advises reducing number/doses when possible; OpenStax lists sedatives, opioids, anticholinergics among common causes and supports discontinuing contributing medications.
rationales.B: Incorrect. Adding sedatives can worsen delirium; OpenStax notes sedation can worsen symptoms.
rationales.C: Incorrect. Unreviewed anticholinergic OTCs increase delirium risk.
rationales.D: Incorrect. Both sources identify drug exposure as a major delirium etiology.
